## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for reading and writing to .pen files and gives you tools to be an expert design generator and validator specifically for web and mobile applications and websites.

- IMPORTANT: The contents of the .pen files are encrypted and can be only access via the "pencil" MCP tools. DO NOT use "Read" or "Grep" tools to read contents of .pen files.
- IMPORTANT: Make sure to ONLY use the "pencil" MCP tools when reading or searching contents of .pen files (batch_get) and making changes inside .pen files (batch_design).
- IMPORTANT: Always follow the tool definitions and formats for the "pencil" MCP tools.

Available tools:
- "get_editor_state({ include_schema })": Start with this tool if you are unaware of the current editor state. Use this tool to determine in the beginning of a task, to understand what is the currently active .pen file you want to work on and the current user selection in it and other essential context information.
- "open_document(filePathOrNew)": When there is no active editor opened, pass 'new' to create an empty .pen file or if the user explicitly ask to open a specific .pen file use its path to open it.
- "get_guidelines(category?, name?, params?)": Load guides and styles for working with .pen files.
- "batch_get(patterns, nodeIds)": Retrieve nodes by searching for matching patterns or by reading node ids in batches. Use this for discovering and understand .pen files.
- "batch_design(operations)": Use it when designing with .pen files to execute multiple insert/copy/update/replace/move/delete/image operations in a single call. The user is asking about whether they can close their terminal windows and still access them within Claude Code (the VSCode extension). Let me think about what they're asking.

They're asking if they can close their external terminal windows and still have access to terminal functionality within Claude Code in VSCode.

The answer is yes - Claude Code in VSCode has its own integrated terminal access via the Bash tool, so they don't need external terminal windows open. Claude Code can execute bash commands directly through the VSCode extension environment.

However, they might also be asking about keeping terminal sessions alive - like if they have processes running in terminals. Let me give a clear, concise answer.

content.text:
Yes. Claude Code runs its own shell sessions via the Bash tool, completely independent of any terminal windows you have open. You can close all your external terminals and I can still run commands, navigate files, and execute anything you need directly from here.

The one caveat: if you have **long-running processes** (like a dev server) currently running in those terminals, closing them will kill those processes. If you need a dev server running in the background, I can start one for you using `run_in_background`.
If I continue chatting in the existing terminal will the conversation from that terminal also appear on the session version of it that exists here in VScode?

content.thinking:
The user is asking whether conversations from an external terminal running Claude Code will sync/appear in the VSCode extension session of Claude Code.

The answer is no - they are separate, independent sessions. Each Claude Code session (whether in a terminal or in VSCode) maintains its own conversation context. They don't share state or sync with each other.

Let me give a clear, concise answer.

content.text:
No. Each Claude Code session is completely independent — the VSCode extension and any terminal instances are separate sessions with their own conversation history. They don't sync or share context with each other.

If you continue a conversation in the terminal, that context stays in the terminal session only. Same goes in reverse.

content.thinking:
The user is showing me two screenshots:
1. The VSCode extension session called "Load in the Basecamp CLI" 
2. A terminal window also running Claude Code in what appears to be the same session "Load in the Basecamp CLI"

Both show the same conversation content - the "What was I doing?" summary about finding Initiate Cancellation tasks. So they're asking if these two are the same session running simultaneously.

Looking more carefully - the VSCode tab is named "Load in the Basecamp CLI" and the terminal window title also says "Load in the Basecamp CLI". The content in both appears to be the same conversation/session.

So it looks like the terminal session and the VSCode session ARE the same session - they're both showing the same conversation. 

Since Claude Code stores sessions on disk, both the terminal and VSCode are reading from the same session file, so they share the same history. They can't both be actively receiving updates in real-time though - changes in one won't immediately appear in the other.

content.text:
Yes — and that actually clarifies something important. Those two are the **same session** ("Load in the Basecamp CLI"), just opened in two different interfaces. Claude Code sessions are stored on disk, so both the terminal and the VSCode extension can read the same session history.

**What this means practically:**

- The history is shared — both show the same past conversation
- But they are **not live-synced** — if you continue typing in the terminal, that new message won't appear in the VSCode session in real time
- If you then open that session in VSCode after sending messages in the terminal, it will reflect the updated history

So you can safely close the terminal and pick up the same session here in VSCode — you won't lose the context. Just click on "Load in the Basecamp CLI" in the sidebar and it's all there.
So I can safely close out every terminal I have open and pickup here?
Yes, exactly. Close them all and pick up right here.
Is there any limitations to using VScode vs the terminal?

A few minor ones worth knowing:

- **No `/terminal` or direct shell access for you** — in the terminal you can type shell commands yourself; here everything goes through me
- **Image input** — you can paste/attach images in VSCode (like you just did), which isn't as easy in the terminal
- **Session switching** — the sidebar makes it easy to jump between sessions; in terminal you'd have to reopen manually
- **Status line** — the terminal shows token count, cache info, and shortcuts at the bottom; VSCode has a cleaner UI but less raw diagnostic info

For practical day-to-day use, VSCode is strictly better or equivalent. The terminal gives slightly more visibility into what's happening under the hood, but nothing you'd miss unless you're debugging Claude Code itself.
